utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Well, I'd met him for the first time that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe how he was dressed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I think that at the time, he was wearing civilian clothes, but the people who were with him were wearing camouflage, NATO uniforms and red berets on their heads, or, rather, on their shoulders, underneath the epaulette.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the vehicle that Frenki Simatovic was driving in, do you recall anything about the licence plate on that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: The car had police licence plates, and it was a jeep. I think it was a Puch-type jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, after you left Belgrade, did there come a time when you arrived at a checkpoint before you arrived at the training camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was this checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: The checkpoint was somewhere just before you get to Ilok, on the road before Ilok.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how many men were at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I noticed, I think, two men. Whether there were any others inside, I don't know, but I did see two armed men.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were those men wearing uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes, they were wearing uniforms, and they had automatic rifles too.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many cars in total, or how many vehicles in total travelled from Belgrade towards the training camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Well, the vehicle in front of me, and I was in the second car.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the vehicle stop at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened at the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: One of those two armed men came up to the jeep. I didn't hear what they said, but he said hello, and he saluted the people in the jeep. He greeted them, I'm sorry, and he just gave me a sign with his hand meaning go through.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So were you checked with -- did you have to produce any documentation or were you stopped or prevented from going through that checkpoint on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Well, I did stop, and it would have been logical for me to show my IDs, but as I was moving along behind the car in front, I was told that as you're going together with them, you can pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, can you describe what happened when the two vehicles arrived in the area of the training camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Well, the two cars didn't arrive at the training camp. We stopped first in front of a house, and there were soldiers there too. But it didn't look like a camp to me. And Mr. Frenki got out there, and so did the people who were with him, and I got up for a short time, and the people who were in uniforms and were armed, standing in front of that house, greeted Frenki, and he told one of them or, rather, he said to me that he would find somebody to take me around, to show me where the men were being trained. And several minutes later, a man in uniform, a young man, took me off a kilometre or so, which is where I visited the people from my town who were attending training there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many armed men were in the vicinity of that house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but there might have been four or five men, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall how they were dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms, and they had those red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did any of those men salute Frenki when he got out of his car or his jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes. The ones who were at the door in front of the house. They did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You were saying that Frenki Simatovic said he would arrange for somebody to take you to the camp. Did there come a time when you actually were taken into the training camp at Ilok?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe what you saw at the training camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: At the very entrance to the training camp there was a ramp, and when they lifted the ramp, I went in, and I was told that it used to be a villa of Tito's and that it was now a makeshift training area. It didn't look like a barracks or a military facility of any kind. And I saw these 20 people from my town. We said hello, we talked for a while. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you learn anything about the identity of any of the instructors present at the camp or who the instructors were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I learned later on that the instructors were members of this special unit of the state security of the MUP of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you learn the identity of any of the instructors present at the camp at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: One of the instructors was this gentleman under number 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you learn the identity of any of the other instructors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I learnt about another one, but he's not on this list here.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to say his name without compromising your identity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that we go briefly into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How long had you spent at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: About an hour, perhaps a little longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if anything, do you recall about the uniforms that the people in the camp were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I remember that these men from my town who were training there were wearing camouflage uniforms with red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see any patches on the uniforms that the men from your town had or on the uniforms of any of the men you saw at the training camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I don't know whether I saw it just then, but later on they wore on those uniforms the patches of the Grey Wolf, the emblem of the Grey Wolf.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "later on," can you be more precise about when it was you saw this Grey Wolf's patch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Upon returning to my town, it was then that I would see those patches on the same uniforms that I saw during that visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 349, tab 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: It is being displayed on the Sanction system on the TV screen before you. I'd ask you to look at that. Do you recognise what's depicted in Prosecution Exhibit 349, tab 12?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes. That is the emblem I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, when you left the camp, did you travel back from the camp alone or once again following Frenki Simatovic's jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I returned alone. I went alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you pass through the same checkpoint that you passed coming to the camp? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe what happened this time you tried to go through the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: They asked me to show my documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And after showing your documents, did you also have a conversation with them regarding what you were doing in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: We didn't talk. They just looked at my documents and told me that I could move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when members of the special unit of the Serbian state security came to the municipality that you're testifying about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: That was on the 11th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you learn about their arrival?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: This gentleman under number 13 informed me that on that day, those men were due to arrive, that we should prepare lunch and accommodation for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did number 13 tell you how many men were arriving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: He said that, in addition to the local men who had gone there for training, that another 30 new men would arrive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he say what the purpose of them, of these 30 men coming to the municipality, what the purpose of their arrival was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: At that point in time, he didn't say why. He just said that they were coming and that they should be provided with lunch and accommodation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time of their arrival, had there been any hostilities in this municipality up until this point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Not any significant conflicts, but there was some minor acts of sabotage in the town and in the immediate vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did these men arrive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: These men arrived in two helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were these police helicopters or military helicopters or civilian helicopters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I think they were military helicopters.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This group of 50 men, what were they wearing, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: They were wearing those camouflage uniforms. On one arm they had the emblem that we just saw of the Grey Wolf, and they wore red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This group of men, did one of them appear to be in charge of the others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And which one was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: The gentleman under number 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, when they arrived, who was present to greet them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Apart from me, there was the local commander of this detachment in that place and two men from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "brigade command," are you referring to the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: The brigade that was stationed in the area, and at the time it was part of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would I be correct in saying that these men were accommodated at a local school before moving to another area still within the municipality you are testifying about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to the takeover of the municipality, were these men ever seen publicly in the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: In the centre of town, as far as I know, they were not, but in the area in which they were put up, in a couple of those villages they did move around openly and they were seen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to identify the names of any of the members of this unit that you can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: To do that, I would ask that we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You testified before about being asked to arrange lunch for these men. Did you arrange such a lunch?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and others from that town organised lunch for them when they arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the course of that lunch, did one of the men indicate his purpose for being there and on behalf of what organisation he was in this municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: One of them said that they had come on behalf of the Serbian Radical Party, for patriotic reasons, to assist the Serbian people in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he or any of the others indicate other areas in which they had previously fought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was at that very luncheon, but later on some of them mentioned that they had been in some other areas where there was combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you recall the locations where they said there had been combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: They mentioned Eastern Slavonia, around Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness now be shown Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 5, and if I might address the Court on this and a series of related exhibits. Your Honours, tabs 5, 6, 12, 14, and 16 are steno notes taken contemporaneously of the interview of five different individuals. These steno notes were taken during questioning by an investigative judge. In the fall of 1992, some of the crimes from this -- or in this municipality were investigated by a military court in Banja Luka, and a number of people were interviewed. The Prosecution is tendering these steno notes based upon several indications of their reliability. First, that the interviews were taken shortly after the events described therein; secondly, the declarations in these interviews are declarations against the self-interest of the respective people who made them. They were recorded stenographically. The witness before the Court has checked and will -- I'm sorry. The stenographic notes were then presented to the declarants and they were given an opportunity to review them and sign them as to their accuracy. And lastly, the details or the substance of these interviews will be corroborated by the witness before the Court who has personal knowledge by -- of these events. The last document from this package of documents related to this investigation is an indictment, and it is tab 10, dated the 5th of January, 1993. Now, as indictments themselves are not evidence, the Prosecution is tendering this particular document for simply two reasons: One, to corroborate biographical information of the first three people who are listed on the indictment; and secondly, as evidence that during this time period, an investigation and the bringing of criminal charges was a possibility at least in one particular instance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. They will be admitted on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask you to take a look at the last page of Prosecution Exhibit 476, tab 5, and my question to you is do you recognise the signature of this person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And whose signature do you recognise that to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: It is the signature of number 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And have you had a chance to review the statement of this person identified as 16 from tab 3? Have you had a chance to review this statement and is it accurate as far as you are able to tell from your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes, I have reviewed this statement several times, and it's mostly accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are there any material inaccuracies that you wish to bring to the Court's attention?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I don't see anything of significance that I would need to pinpoint for the Court. I think that it is mostly correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The statement makes reference to - and I ask you, do you know from your personal knowledge whether this person identified as number 16 - 16 received two vehicles for his participation in the events of this municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: The question is whether that is true? Is that the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that this person under this number received those two vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what types of vehicles did this person receive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: A passenger vehicle, a Mercedes, and a Golf passenger vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was his receipt of -- I'm sorry. Do you know generally from where these two vehicles came? Not so much the particular identity of the individual owners, but do you know what the source was of these two vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: The owners were Croats or Muslims, and this was considered to be war booty.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was the Crisis Staff, the Serbian Crisis Staff, aware of number 16 receiving these two vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did they give official permission to him for having these vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no official document, but orally he was given permission to drive those two vehicles away.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were there any other members of the group that arrived from Serbia that also were given permission to take vehicles that you've described as coming from war booty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection. Mr. Groome is referring to this number 16 as being a person from Serbia, and from the court documents it is clear that the person was treated as a citizen of Republika Srpska, that is, of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Therefore, the question is put in a way as to distort the facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will be able to consider where it was that he really came from. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, to the best of your knowledge, where was this person identified as number 16, where was he from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: That person is from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know the particular town in Serbia he was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I do know from which town he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, could you get him to explain what he means by "war booty."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may just clear up this particular point first, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Prior to number 16 being involved in the events you're describing now with the war booty, had he had any other contacts or any other presence in the municipality you're testifying about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Until the 11th of April, 1992, as far as I know, he hadn't been in that area. I think he didn't even come to visit that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Judge Robinson is asking you to describe in greater detail, what do you mean when you use the term "war booty"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: After combat operations which were conducted in this particular case if we're talking about these two vehicles, those vehicles stayed behind in the area after combat operations and then the soldiers who were in the area picked up the vehicles and brought them to the territory of the municipality and then a record was made of these vehicles coming from different -- from another area, including other property of any value that was found in the area that had been liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that this property, including the cars, was property that was left by either people that were killed during the takeover of the municipality or by people that fled the municipality and left their property behind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I don't know. I think specifically regarding these two vehicles, the people were not there. They simply withdrew after the operations in that village. This wasn't in a town. It was in a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask we go into closed session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to the 15th of April, 1992. Did you attend a meeting on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us who else was present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: At that meeting number 9 was present, number 10, number 13. Later, number 16 arrived too, and perhaps a couple of other men.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Aside from number 16, were there any other representatives of the Serbian DB present at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1244
utterances.text: I think not.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, before going into the substance of the meeting, is this a convenient place for the court to adjourn?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn now. Two matters: For the press, I'm asked to remind you not to refer to the municipality, anything which might identify the municipality in this case. Secondly, Witness B-1244, we're going to adjourn for the night. Could you be back, please, tomorrow at 9.00 to continue your evidence. Could you remember during it not to speak to anybody about it until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. Very well. We'll adjourn now until tomorrow morning.
